turns.en: Nothing to eat or drink after midnight, alright? They'll come for you about nine. You'll need to take your jewellery off and pop this gown on.
turns.cy: Dim byd i'w fwyta nac i'w yfed ar ôl hanner nos, iawn? Mi ddôn nhw i'ch nôl chi tua naw. Mi fydd raid i chi dynnu'ch gemwaith a rhoi'r ŵn 'ma amdanoch.
chunks: Nothing to eat or drink after midnight, alright?
Dim byd i'w fwyta nac i'w yfed ar ôl hanner nos, iawn?
the i'w frame repeats on each verb — Welsh cannot coordinate two verbal nouns under one particle
They'll come for you about nine
Mi ddôn nhw i'ch nôl chi tua naw
English's 'come for' relocates to dod i nôl, 'come to fetch'
You'll need to take your jewellery off and pop this gown on
Mi fydd raid i chi dynnu'ch gemwaith a rhoi'r ŵn 'ma amdanoch
the impersonal obligation frame; both English particle verbs collapse, and 'on' becomes the conjugated amdanoch

turns.en: Right you are. Nothing after midnight.
turns.cy: O'r gorau. Dim byd ar ôl hanner nos.
chunks: Dim byd ar ôl hanner nos

turns.en: Good. Someone will come first thing to put a name band on and go through the checklist with you.
turns.cy: Da iawn. Mi ddaw rhywun peth cynta i roi band enw amdanoch chi ac i fynd drwy'r rhestr efo chi.
chunks: to put a name band on
i roi band enw amdanoch chi
English's particle 'on' becomes the conjugated preposition amdanoch chi
and go through the checklist with you
ac i fynd drwy'r rhestr efo chi
the purpose i must be restated — Welsh does not coordinate under one particle

turns.en: Understood. My son's bringing my dressing gown in tonight anyway.
turns.cy: Dallt. Mae fy mab i'n dod â fy ngŵn nos i mewn heno, beth bynnag.
chunks: My son's bringing my dressing gown in tonight anyway
Mae fy mab i'n dod â fy ngŵn nos i mewn heno, beth bynnag
Welsh 'bring' is the â-carrying frame dod â

turns.en: Perfect. Any worries in the night, ring the bell - the night staff know all about tomorrow.
turns.cy: Perffaith. Unrhyw bryderon yn y nos, canwch y gloch — mae'r staff nos yn gwybod y cwbl am fory.
chunks: 'any' → unrhyw in the free-choice topic, against rhywbeth in offers (S9)
the night staff know all about tomorrow
mae'r staff nos yn gwybod y cwbl am fory

turns.en: Thank you, love. I feel better knowing what's what.
turns.cy: Diolch, del. Dw i'n teimlo'n well o wybod be ydy be.
chunks: I feel better knowing what's what
Dw i'n teimlo'n well o wybod be ydy be
the causal o + verbal noun, as at 'knowing that's there'

turns.en: Nothing to eat or drink after midnight. They'll come for you about nine.
turns.cy: Dim byd i'w fwyta nac i'w yfed ar ôl hanner nos. Mi ddôn nhw i'ch nôl chi tua naw.
chunks: Nothing to eat or drink after midnight
Dim byd i'w fwyta nac i'w yfed ar ôl hanner nos
⚠ line — the nil-by-mouth instruction, plainest possible
They'll come for you about nine
Mi ddôn nhw i'ch nôl chi tua naw

turns.en: What about my heart tablets? Do I still take those in the morning?
turns.cy: Be am fy nhabledi calon i? Ydw i'n dal i gymryd y rheiny yn y bore?
chunks: Be am fy nhabledi calon i?
⚠ line — the nasal mutation after fy absorbed
Do I still take those in the morning?
Ydw i'n dal i gymryd y rheiny yn y bore?
⚠ line — 'still' → dal i, the same frame as 'keep -ing'

turns.en: Good question. Some tablets you still take with a tiny sip of water, and some we hold. I'll check your chart with the doctor tonight and write it down for you, so there's no guessing in the morning.
turns.cy: Cwestiwn da. Mae rhai tabledi dach chi'n dal i'w cymryd efo llymaid bach o ddŵr, ac mae rhai dan ni'n eu dal yn ôl. Mi wna i tsiecio'ch siart chi efo'r doctor heno ac ysgrifennu'r cwbl i lawr i chi, fel nad oes 'na ddyfalu yn y bore.
chunks: ⚠ line — the English indefinite article erases
Some tablets you still take with a tiny sip of water
Mae rhai tabledi dach chi'n dal i'w cymryd efo llymaid bach o ddŵr
⚠ line — English's topicalised object needs a Welsh existential to hang on
ac mae rhai dan ni'n eu dal yn ôl
⚠ line — English's bare 'hold' is clinical shorthand; Welsh spells it dal yn ôl so the instruction cannot be misread
I'll check your chart with the doctor tonight
Mi wna i tsiecio'ch siart chi efo'r doctor heno
and write it down for you
ac ysgrifennu'r cwbl i lawr i chi
so there's no guessing in the morning
fel nad oes 'na ddyfalu yn y bore
the fel bod frame over a negative existential

turns.en: Written down would be lovely. I don't trust my memory these days.
turns.cy: Mi fasa'i gael o wedi'i sgwennu i lawr yn hyfryd. Dw i ddim yn trystio fy nghof y dyddiau yma.
chunks: Mi fasa'i gael o wedi'i sgwennu i lawr yn hyfryd
⚠ line — English's bare participle cannot be a Welsh subject; it needs a 'having it written' clause under it
I don't trust my memory these days
Dw i ddim yn trystio fy nghof y dyddiau yma

turns.en: Leave it with me - it'll be there in black and white by your bed.
turns.cy: Gadwch o efo fi — mi fydd o yna'n ddu a gwyn wrth ymyl eich gwely chi.
chunks: it'll be there in black and white by your bed
mi fydd o yna'n ddu a gwyn wrth ymyl eich gwely chi
⚠ line — the black-and-white idiom runs the same way in Welsh

turns.en: Thank you. That's one less thing to fret about.
turns.cy: Diolch. Dyna un peth yn llai i boeni amdano fo.
chunks: That's one less thing to fret about
Dyna un peth yn llai i boeni amdano fo
Welsh puts the comparative after the noun — 'one thing less' — and 'fret about' conjugates as amdano fo

turns.en: Nothing to eat or drink after midnight, and you'll pop this gown on in the morning.
turns.cy: Dim byd i'w fwyta nac i'w yfed ar ôl hanner nos, ac mi rowch chi'r ŵn 'ma amdanoch yn y bore.
chunks: Nothing to eat or drink after midnight
Dim byd i'w fwyta nac i'w yfed ar ôl hanner nos
and you'll pop this gown on in the morning
ac mi rowch chi'r ŵn 'ma amdanoch yn y bore

turns.en: I'm ever so nervous. Will I be asleep for the whole thing?
turns.cy: Dw i mor nerfus. Fydda i'n cysgu drwy'r cwbl?
chunks: English's intensifier 'ever so' has no Welsh reflex — mor carries it alone
Will I be asleep for the whole thing?
Welsh has no adjective 'asleep' here — it uses the verb, so the state becomes an activity

turns.en: You'll be asleep for all of it, and someone's with you every single minute. Nervous is completely normal.
turns.cy: Mi fyddwch chi'n cysgu drwy'r cwbl, ac mi fydd rhywun efo chi bob munud. Mae bod yn nerfus yn hollol normal.
chunks: You'll be asleep for all of it
Mi fyddwch chi'n cysgu drwy'r cwbl
and someone's with you every single minute
ac mi fydd rhywun efo chi bob munud
English's emphatic 'single' erases — bob carries it
Mae bod yn nerfus yn hollol normal
a bare adjective cannot be a Welsh subject; bod yn must be built under it

turns.en: Every minute? And how long does it take, all in?
turns.cy: Bob munud? A faint o amser mae o'n gymryd, i gyd?
chunks: And how long does it take, all in?
A faint o amser mae o'n gymryd, i gyd?
Welsh asks 'how much of time'; the resumptive mutation on gymryd is obligatory

turns.en: About an hour, then a couple of hours coming round with us keeping an eye on you. You'll be back on the ward for lunch.
turns.cy: Rhyw awr, wedyn rhyw ddwyawr yn dod atoch chi'ch hun a ninnau'n cadw golwg arnoch chi. Mi fyddwch chi'n ôl ar y ward erbyn cinio.
chunks: the indefinite article erases; rhyw carries the approximation
then a couple of hours coming round
wedyn rhyw ddwyawr yn dod atoch chi'ch hun
English's 'come round' from anaesthesia relocates to dod atoch chi'ch hun, 'come to yourself'
with us keeping an eye on you
a ninnau'n cadw golwg arnoch chi
English's absolute 'with X -ing' relocates to the conjunctive pronoun a ninnau
You'll be back on the ward for lunch
Mi fyddwch chi'n ôl ar y ward erbyn cinio

turns.en: Back for lunch. Right. That helps, that does.
turns.cy: Yn ôl erbyn cinio. Reit. Mae hynna'n helpu, ydy.
chunks: English's emphatic right-dislocation with a dummy 'does' becomes the Welsh verb-echo ydy
